content:
Apple Podcasts is my go-to podcast app, but for a long time I've been unhappy with its core "Up Next" queue feature. I'm happy to share that iOS 27.2 brings the solution.

iOS 27.2 splits Apple Podcasts' "Up Next" queue into two sections: "New Episodes" and "Keep Listening"

There's a lot to appreciate about Apple Podcasts. Transcripts and auto-generated chapters are two killer features that make this app my favourite. I love all the recent video-related upgrades too.

But for years, Apple Podcasts' core 'Up Next' queue has often made me want to switch to another app.

I've written before about why the 'Up Next' feature is flawed. In short:

  • It makes it hard to see clearly what new shows you can listen to
  • Episodes easily disappear, even if you're halfway through listening

But I'm thrilled to share that iOS 27.2 finally brings the long-awaited fix to 'Up Next'. The method is to split this feature into two separate sections:

  • New Episodes
  • Keep Listening

At the top of the app is 'New Episodes', which looks and works much the same as 'Up Next'. As the name suggests, it shows only the latest episode of every show you follow.

'Keep Listening' sits right below it, serving as a central hub where you can find all the episodes you've started but haven't finished.

Top comment by Nutmac

Playlist management is still a mess, and the inability to sync across devices is baffling.

Together, these two sections solve all my major problems with the old 'Up Next' queue.

You can easily see at a glance what's new, and I've lost track of episodes, because anything I start listening to appears in 'Keep Listening'. I still have some minor quibbles, but these changes alone have resolved my main issues with 'Up Next'.

If you haven't tried Apple Podcasts in a while, iOS 27.2 is a great time to give it another go.

Do you use Apple or another podcast app? Feel free to share with us in the comments.
